motion: Our city should move municipal staff to a four-day, 32-hour work week.

propositions.text: A four-day week keeps output per employee roughly the same.
It would meaningfully improve staff retention.
Residents would face reduced access to services.
Services can be kept open five days with staggered shifts.
Trial programmes elsewhere were run in comparable public-sector settings.
Hiring more staff to cover gaps would raise costs.

arguments.author: Rae
arguments.text: If output stays flat and retention goes up, the change is clearly worth it — and pilots show output does stay flat.

arguments.author: Sam
arguments.text: Staggered shifts mean the public never notices the difference.

arguments.author: Jo
arguments.text: Either service access drops or we hire more people; both are unacceptable, so we shouldn't do it.

arguments.author: Lee
arguments.text: The pilot results don't transfer: they weren't public sector, so we can't assume output holds, and without that the case fails.

arguments.author: Rae
arguments.text: Staggered shifts work, and if they work access doesn't drop, so access will drop for no one.
